lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.19 - A Find the 8 hidden pictures

details: Find 8 hidden pictures strengthens recognition of written words and hidden visuals.
Look for word and visual recognition of vocabulary, and neat circling in the picture.
“Guess what? We’re having a party! We need tasty food for the party and stationery to make our invitations. Let’s look carefully at the picture and find the things we need.”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.19 - B. Listen and match

details: Listen and match checks students’ understanding of ‘has got + vocabulary item’ using visuals. Students practise listening for specific information and matching to an image.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices and straight lines..
“Great! Let’s split into teams — Team 1 will make the invitations, and Team 2 will get the food. Listen carefully and match the things each student has got for their job.”

Heads Together:

Reward moment

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.73 - A Follow the path

details: Follow the path combines students’’ ability to recognise written words and visuals in a sequence from different vocabulary sets.
Look for accurate choices in the repetition of the sequence and clear lines with good penmanship.

“Before we start preparing, we need to practise saying all the words. What have you got? What do you want? Let’s read, follow the clues, and tick the right answers so we can name everything for our party.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.20 - Speaking Toss a Coin Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer creates semi-controlled practice for students in the form of a visually based board game.
Look for confident use of ‘What do you want? What have you got’ questions and clear sentence answers.
“It’s party time! Let’s play our speaking game to check we’ve got everything we need. How do you feel? Are you excited? Ask and answer your questions — the party is starting!”
